original_question: Given an abelian variety A, does there exist an algebraic curve C such that A is isogenous to the Jacobian of C?
target_in_paper: Question (8.0.1), sharpened by the existence statement Y^(cu)(k,g) in §8.1.4 and by the discussion that the genuinely open case is over countable algebraically closed fields; the paper also proposes a Newton-polygon route via §8.5.1 and Expectation (8.5.4). ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the core relation in the paper: an abelian variety A, an algebraic curve C, and the requirement that A be isogenous to the Jacobian of C. That is exactly the relation posed in the introductory Question (8.0.1). ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))
missing_details: The paper does not leave the base field implicit: one works over a fixed field k, typically algebraically closed, and the genuinely unresolved case emphasized in the paper is for countable algebraically closed fields (especially the algebraic closure of Q), not for C. ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))

The dimension g = dim(A) matters. The problem is already settled positively for g <= 3, so the interesting range is g >= 4. ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))

The paper broadens 'curve' to 'curve of compact type' when formulating the moduli-theoretic version, because these are exactly the stable curves whose Jacobians are abelian varieties and whose moduli define the closed Torelli locus. ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))
The isogeny is considered as an isogeny of abelian varieties, without requiring compatibility with a polarization. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~pries/Preprints/14hp1113.pdf))

The paper's actual research emphasis is not to decide the question for an arbitrary given A, but to ask whether there exists some abelian variety of dimension g whose isogeny class avoids all Jacobians of curves of compact type. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~pries/Preprints/14hp1113.pdf))

As stated, the draft sounds uniformly open, but the paper explains that over C counterexamples already exist for every g >= 4; the open part is the countable-field version. ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))
refined_question: Let k be a countable algebraically closed field, for example the algebraic closure of Q, and let g >= 4. Does there exist an abelian variety A over k of dimension g such that A is not isogenous, as an unpolarized abelian variety, to the Jacobian J(C) of any curve C of compact type over k?
justification: The draft matches the paper's introductory Question (8.0.1), but the nearby context immediately narrows the mathematically interesting version: §8.1.3 disposes of g <= 3, the introduction records that counterexamples exist over C for g >= 4, and the paper then treats the countable-field case as the real open problem. The Newton-polygon discussion in §8.5 is presented precisely as a possible strategy for proving the existence statement Y^(cu)(k,g), i.e. the existence of an abelian variety not isogenous to any Jacobian of a curve of compact type. ([123dok.net](https://123dok.net/document/q05j5rjx-problems-workshop-automorphisms-curves-leiden-august.html))

citations.label: (8.1.1) Jacobians; (8.1.2) Torelli locus; (8.1.3) positive answer for 1 <= g <= 3
(8.3.1) existence over C for g >= 4; (8.3.4) open over countable fields
